input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional election to terminate the Agreement by written notice, with service (and therefore the Agreement) ending on the last day of the month following the notice month — i.e. roughly 30-60 days. That is a Customer convenience right on notice shorter than the 60-90 day fallback window, and no early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere (compensation under Section 5 is invoiced monthly in arrears, so there are no prepaid fees to refund), which is better than the fallback's three-months-of-fees cap. TrueLink has no convenience termination right at all during the term: Section 13 only allows Sections 2 and 3 to end for Client breach/default under the System or Credit Repository Agreements, and the 30-day non-renewal notice in Section 13 is a natural-term non-renewal mechanic that belongs under RENEWAL, not a mid-term Vendor convenience right. The initial term is one year with successive one-year renewals, so there is no multi-year lock-in without an exit. The bargain therefore meets the fallback on every material term and effectively matches preferred on the Vendor-side elements; the only shortfalls against preferred wording are that the Client's exit can take up to about 60 rather than 30 days and there is no express pro-rata prepaid-fee refund sentence (immaterial given monthly arrears billing). We note these in passing and do not redline. One drafting point worth a non-substantive query: Section 14's "Subject to Section 4" and Section 2(c)'s cross-reference to "section 12" are stale references (termination is Section 14).
